# ShaderLOD PC test handoff

This build targets **Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.253 and Java 21**. It contains
the current applicable optimization ports and independent controls for all nine
pinned shader families. Performance and visual acceptance belong to the RTX 5080
test phase; the Mac's previous winning configurations are not PC presets.

## Install

Use a separate clean Minecraft instance. Copy the package's `mods` contents into
its `mods` folder and the original `shaderpacks` contents into `shaderpacks`.
Keep one ShaderLOD JAR. The included Iris 1.8.12 and Sodium 0.6.13 are unmodified,
checksum-pinned release files; `manifest.json` records their exact bytes and
source URLs. Do not install the development observer mod.

Start without Distant Horizons or extra resource/performance mods. These are
separate compatibility checks after the clean baseline. Existing source, API,
material and resource guards retain native behavior when they cannot qualify a
particular configuration.

Load each original shader in Iris and check that it renders normally before
tuning. Preserve its native AA and other quality choices. The package retains
the upstream ZIPs and their license notices without modifying them.

| Shader | Pinned version |
|---|---|
| Photon | 1.3b |
| Complementary Reimagined | r5.9.3 |
| Complementary Unbound | r5.9.3 |
| BSL | 10.1.8 |
| MakeUp UltraFast | 9.5g |
| Sildur's Vibrant | 2.02 Extreme |
| Solas | 3.7b |
| Bliss | 2.1.2 |
| AstraLex | 93.0 |

## Tune each shader

1. Select the shader and save its native settings. Save and quit the current
   world, then open **ShaderLOD benchmark** from the title screen.
2. Choose **Full inventory (60 min/segment)** for the main test. It opens the
   mod's separate, repeatable benchmark world. Keep the game focused, with no
   menus open, and avoid other GPU-heavy work during sampling.
3. Read the final result. **SAVED** requires fresh combined native-relative
   validation. **INCOMPLETE** is not a winning result. Full coverage and saved
   performance validation are separate: a completed inventory pass can still
   produce no accepted improvement.
4. If the result says **PARTIAL_RESUMABLE**, run Full again with the same shader,
   native options, build and clean benchmark setup. Completed candidate coverage
   can continue; old timing measurements are never reused. Source, option,
   hardware or inventory changes start new coverage. An independent manual
   profile change also starts a new campaign.
5. Use **Results folder** to retain that shader's fresh result directory. Repeat
   for the next original shader; requested configurations are scoped by family.

**Quick partial search (5 minutes)** is a short sanity check. It does not examine
the complete inventory. Full is a finite, resumable candidate pass, not an
exhaustive search of every possible feature combination. An external resource
pack makes Full single-segment because its ID does not prove unchanged contents.

The tuner turns VSync off and selects Minecraft's **unlimited** setting during
sampling. The exported value `260` is this version's unlimited sentinel, not a
260 FPS ceiling. Original video settings are restored afterward. Actual GPU
query timings are recorded where supported; unavailable values remain empty.

## Interpreting feature coverage

The inventory has 61 canonical control IDs. A shader does not necessarily have
61 distinct applicable algorithms. The [readiness matrix](READINESS.md) records native effects
or kernels that are absent, existing equivalent controls, and unqualified
research prototypes. Full explicitly records skipped, inactive, refused and
inconclusive cases rather than counting them as independently timed work.

Native-disabled effects remain disabled. For example, default Bliss has material
POM and screen-space specular reflections off; Complementary's material POM needs
the appropriate RP profile; Sildur material POM needs `nMap=2`. Enable a native
effect only if you want to test that shader configuration, then start a new pass.
A requested or timed flag does not prove active pixels or reduced GPU work.

The DH terrain-radius control remains available for manual testing. It requires
warm, inspected, explicitly confirmed DH coverage. Every automatic tuner Apply
revokes that confirmation, so automatic tuning reports
`MANUAL_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and skips it; it never invents visual coverage.

## Cancel, recovery and review

**Cancel tuning** restores the campaign's original profile and releases its
simulation ownership. **Undo last tune** restores the original profile/video
state, including after a saved result. A resumed Full campaign retains its first
original recovery state. If restoration is pending, retry Undo before another
tune or leaving the demo; the job keeps ownership until recovery is acknowledged.
After a client interruption, the persistent recovery journal must be resolved
with Undo before a new tune can start.

After each useful result, inspect near/far transitions, moving foliage and thin
geometry, shadows, water/reflections, moving camera and temporal accumulation.
Compare native Off/Quality against the selected profile in ordinary worlds too.
Then test your PBR resource packs and Distant Horizons separately. A statistical
SAVED result does not certify visual equivalence.

Photon, Solas and AstraLex have stock shader/driver failures on this Mac. Their
source ports and recovery contracts were checked here; their first successful
PC driver rendering remains part of your test. Keep the exact result directory,
`logs/latest.log`, a crash report if produced, and screenshots of any defect.

## Scene recovery source context

The exact lease implementation is SceneLease (source-checkout reference: `../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/SceneLease.java:45`; not bundled), not BenchmarkWorld. `prepare` permits only a private singleplayer server with one player. `freeze` captures its prior frozen state in the submitted server task before freezing. `close` sets cancellation, submits restoration of that captured state on the same server, then waits up to two seconds on the task future; it marks the lease closed only after that future completes normally. Timeout or exceptional completion throws and leaves ownership retained; retry reuses an unfinished restoration future or replaces an exceptionally completed one. This is an actual server-task completion barrier in the source, not a fire-and-forget request.

AutoTuner.restoreOwnedState (source-checkout reference: `../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/AutoTuner.java:498`; not bundled) first requires the exact original source/current family, restores core/preset through public Apply, restores the original independent flags through the guarded edit transaction, and restores video. It then closes the lease, nulls the lease only after successful close, and writes `RESTORED` through the journal. restore (source-checkout reference: `../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/AutoTuner.java:478`; not bundled) clears the Job only when that whole recovery operation returns COMPLETE. A failed close keeps its lease reference and throws; retries park after three failures with PENDING recovery and the Job retained. Normal terminal finish (source-checkout reference: `../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/AutoTuner.java:437`; not bundled) also closes the lease before journal completion and Job release.

TuningJournal (source-checkout reference: `../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/TuningJournal.java:15`; not bundled) writes the original `PENDING` Undo state atomically before `Job.start` prepares/freezes the scene. Both retained `undo-original.properties` files contain `state=PENDING`; the cancelled run metadata contains `result=RESTORED`, and the later status is inactive and world-ready. These retained runtime artifacts, combined with the compiled implementation ordering above, support successful source-context recovery through the server-task completion barrier. The prior paragraph's telemetry caveat means **no separately captured physical simulation-tick snapshot or explicit acknowledgement event**, not an absent acknowledgement barrier in the implementation. We did not directly measure resumed tick advancement or independently read back the server frozen state after close. The naturally INCOMPLETE second run uses the same close-before-terminal ordering. No new runtime action or test was performed for this clarification; commands are released.

# Deeper verification and reusable tunings — October 17, 2026

Scope is **Minecraft 1.21.1 NeoForge, all nine pinned shader families**. This phase found and repaired two real activation/fidelity defects, made named tunings reproduce their requested configuration, and exercised normal Apply/Undo, durable recovery and tuner continuation in the game. It produced **no new SAVED performance winner**. Source support, linked driver source, affected pixels, visual fidelity and speed remain separate claims.

Requested named-effect settings are retained even where a particular family has no matching consumer; saving them does not establish that every effect group acts on every shader. /shaderlod tune start
/shaderlod tune start 300
/shaderlod tune full
/shaderlod tune status
/shaderlod tune cancel
/shaderlod tune undo

/shaderlod tune demo exit

# ShaderLOD PC test handoff

This build targets **Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.253 and Java 21**. It contains
the current applicable optimization ports and independent controls for all nine
pinned shader families. Performance and visual acceptance belong to the RTX 5080
test phase; the Mac's previous winning configurations are not PC presets.

## Install

Use a separate clean Minecraft instance. Copy the package's `mods` contents into
its `mods` folder and the original `shaderpacks` contents into `shaderpacks`.
Keep one ShaderLOD JAR. The included Iris 1.8.12 and Sodium 0.6.13 are unmodified,
checksum-pinned release files; `SOURCE_PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json` records their exact bytes and
source URLs. Do not install the development observer mod.

Start without Distant Horizons or extra resource/performance mods. These are
separate compatibility checks after the clean baseline. Existing source, API,
material and resource guards retain native behavior when they cannot qualify a
particular configuration.

Load each original shader in Iris and check that it renders normally before
tuning. Preserve its native AA and other quality choices. The package retains
the upstream ZIPs and their license notices without modifying them.

| Shader | Pinned version |
|---|---|
| Photon | 1.3b |
| Complementary Reimagined | r5.9.3 |
| Complementary Unbound | r5.9.3 |
| BSL | 10.1.8 |
| MakeUp UltraFast | 9.5g |
| Sildur's Vibrant | 2.02 Extreme |
| Solas | 3.7b |
| Bliss | 2.1.2 |
| AstraLex | 93.0 |

## Tune each shader

1. Select the shader and save its native settings. Save and quit the current
   world, then open **ShaderLOD benchmark** from the title screen.
2. Choose a tuning goal, then **Full inventory (60 min/segment)** for the main test. It opens the
   mod's separate, repeatable benchmark world. Keep the game focused, with no
   menus open, and avoid other GPU-heavy work during sampling.
3. Read the final result. **SAVED** requires fresh combined native-relative
   validation. **INCOMPLETE** is not a winning result. Full coverage and saved
   performance validation are separate: a completed inventory pass can still
   produce no accepted improvement.
4. If the result says **PARTIAL_RESUMABLE**, run Full again with the same shader,
   native options, build and clean benchmark setup. Completed candidate coverage
   can continue; old timing measurements are never reused. Source, option,
   hardware or inventory changes start new coverage. An independent manual
   profile change also starts a new campaign.
5. Open **Saved tunings** to name or rename an accepted result. You can also
   save any current configuration as a manual preset, even without a timing win.
   Export selected to retain its portable JSON and any intact local measurement
   evidence. See [Saved tunings](SAVED_TUNINGS.md) for Apply/Undo and import.
6. Use **Results folder** to retain that shader's fresh result directory. Repeat
   for the next original shader; requested configurations are scoped by family.

Performance, Balanced and Quality are separate searches. Run each desired goal
for each shader; a result from one goal is not measured evidence for another.
Quality search allows only the reviewed exact changes and is distinct from
the original native Quality setting. No goal is guaranteed to find an improvement.

**Quick partial search (5 minutes)** is a short sanity check. It does not examine
the complete inventory. Full is a finite, resumable candidate pass, not an
exhaustive search of every possible feature combination. An external resource
pack makes Full single-segment because its ID does not prove unchanged contents.

The tuner turns VSync off and selects Minecraft's **unlimited** setting during
sampling. The exported value `260` is this version's unlimited sentinel, not a
260 FPS ceiling. Original video settings are restored afterward. Actual GPU
query timings are recorded where supported; unavailable values remain empty.

## Interpreting feature coverage

The inventory has 61 canonical control IDs. A shader does not necessarily have
61 distinct applicable algorithms. The readiness matrix records native effects
or kernels that are absent, existing equivalent controls, and unqualified
research prototypes. Full explicitly records skipped, inactive, refused and
inconclusive cases rather than counting them as independently timed work.

Native-disabled effects remain disabled. For example, default Bliss has material
POM and screen-space specular reflections off; Complementary's material POM needs
the appropriate RP profile; Sildur material POM needs `nMap=2`. Enable a native
effect only if you want to test that shader configuration, then start a new pass.
A requested or timed flag does not prove active pixels or reduced GPU work.

The DH terrain-radius control remains available for manual testing. It requires
warm, inspected, explicitly confirmed DH coverage. Every automatic tuner Apply
revokes that confirmation, so automatic tuning reports
`MANUAL_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and skips it; it never invents visual coverage.

## Cancel, recovery and review

**Cancel tuning** restores the campaign's original profile and releases its
simulation ownership. **Undo last tune** restores the original profile/video
state, including after a saved result. A resumed Full campaign retains its first
original recovery state. If restoration is pending, retry Undo before another
tune or leaving the demo; the job keeps ownership until recovery is acknowledged.
After a client interruption, the persistent recovery journal must be resolved
with Undo before a new tune can start.

After each useful result, inspect near/far transitions, moving foliage and thin
geometry, shadows, water/reflections, moving camera and temporal accumulation.
Compare native Off/Quality against the selected profile in ordinary worlds too.
Then test your PBR resource packs and Distant Horizons separately. A statistical
SAVED result does not certify visual equivalence.

Photon, Solas and AstraLex have stock shader/driver failures on this Mac. Their
source ports and recovery contracts were checked here; their first successful
PC driver rendering remains part of your test. Keep the exact result directory,
`logs/latest.log`, a crash report if produced, and screenshots of any defect.

This separate test instance uses the unchanged verified ShaderLOD main mod, original shaders and an optional thin remote-controller variant of shaderlod_dev. It contains no research mixins or benchmark substitutes.

Use Java21. Open the instance and leave it at the title screen. Remote owner will confirm actual5080 renderer, native options/focus and recovery before Full runs. Do not use the PC for other GPU work during measurement. Full runs are finite60-minute segments; coverage may need continuation. No accepted improvement is guaranteed. Visual review remains separate.

The helper reads only .minecraft/shaderlod-remote/request.json and writes request-ID receipts. It is opt-in via -Dshaderlod.pcControl=true. Normal shutdown requires successful restoration and world-save completion; it never kills unrelated Java processes. No commands are queued in this instance.
